sourcedFrom: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 (2025)
cleanIntro: Ruger's own procedure for the LCR .357, from PM199. The strip is short by design — grip off, and no further.

steps.title: Confirm the revolver is unloaded
steps.action: Press the crane latch, swing the cylinder out, and confirm every chamber is empty by eye and by finger.
steps.prose: A revolver has as many chambers as it has holes. Check all of them, not just the one under the hammer.
steps.quote: BE CERTAIN THE REVOLVER IS UNLOADED BEFORE DISASSEMBLY.
steps.cite: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 — Disassembly, step 1, p.22
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly or assembly. Never remove or install a loaded cylinder - it can fire if dropped or struck.

steps.title: Know what this one is chambered for
steps.action: The .357 gun will also chamber .38 Special and .38 Special +P.
steps.prose: Same frame, same strip, wider chambering — which means more to clean out of the chambers after a mixed session.
steps.quote: 357 is chambered for the .357 Magnum cartridge, and can also chamber the .38 Special and .38 Special + P.
steps.cite: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 — General Information and Mechanical Characteristics, p.11

steps.title: Take the grip off
steps.action: With a properly fitting screwdriver, remove the grip retaining screw from the bottom of the grip, then slide the grip down off the fire control housing.
steps.prose: Properly fitting matters — an undersized bit rounds this screw, and it is the only fastener on the gun you will touch.
steps.quote: Using a properly fitting screwdriver, remove the grip retaining screw from bottom of grip. Slide the grip down off fire control housing
steps.cite: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 — Disassembly, step 2, p.22

steps.title: That is the whole strip
steps.action: Stop here. Grip off is the entire disassembly Ruger publishes for this revolver.
steps.prose: Nothing else comes apart for cleaning, and Ruger is explicit about who may go further.
steps.quote: Further disassembly is not required for normal cleaning purposes. Any further disassembly should only be undertaken by trained factory service personnel.
steps.cite: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 — Disassembly, step 3, p.22

deepSteps.title: Why this is a separate job
deepSteps.action: Ruger documents one procedure past the field strip: lubricating the hammer and hammer pivot pin, on an interval.
deepSteps.prose: This is not part of routine cleaning. It has its own schedule and its own risk.
deepSteps.quote: It is recommended that the hammer and hammer pivot pin be lubricated approximately every 1,000 rounds of firing (live or dry fire).
deepSteps.cite: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 — Lubricating Hammer and Hammer Pivot Pin, p.24

deepSteps.title: Open it up and orient it
deepSteps.action: Check the firearm is unloaded, open the cylinder, remove the grip, then turn the revolver so the shooter's right-hand side is up.
deepSteps.prose: The oil goes in from the right side; getting the orientation right before you start is what lets gravity do the work.
deepSteps.quote: Orient firearm so the shooter's right hand side of the firearm is up.
deepSteps.cite: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 — Lubricating Hammer and Hammer Pivot Pin, step 4, p.24

deepSteps.title: Push the hammer pivot pin — partway
deepSteps.action: With a small punch, 1/8 inch or smaller, gently push the hammer pivot pin until it is recessed about .10 inch deep.
deepSteps.prose: Partway. The pin is being moved just far enough to clear its pocket, and no further.
deepSteps.caution: DO NOT COMPLETELY REMOVE PIN OR YOUR REVOLVER WILL CEASE TO FUNCTION.
deepSteps.quote: Using a small (1/8" or smaller) punch, gently push on hammer pivot pin until the pin is recessed about .10" deep
deepSteps.cite: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 — Lubricating Hammer and Hammer Pivot Pin, step 5, p.24
deepSteps.warn: DO NOT COMPLETELY REMOVE PIN OR YOUR REVOLVER WILL CEASE TO FUNCTION.

deepSteps.title: Oil it, and let it drain in
deepSteps.action: Put 2 to 3 drops of a polymer-safe firearm oil or cleaner-lubricant-protectant into the hammer pivot hole on the shooter's right-hand side.
deepSteps.prose: Let it drain down around the pin and into the action. Rotating the exposed pin head on the left side helps it travel.
deepSteps.quote: Apply 2 to 3 drops of any standard commercial, polymer-safe firearm oil or standard commercial, polymer-safe cleaner-lubricant-protectant to the hammer pivot hole on the shooter's right hand side of the firearm
deepSteps.cite: Ruger LCR and LCRx Instruction Manual — PM199 — Lubricating Hammer and Hammer Pivot Pin, step 6, p.24

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Release and swing out the cylinder, and be sure all cartridges and cases are out
Clean the barrel from the muzzle end, taking care to avoid damaging the muzzle crown
Soak the bore: run a properly sized solvent-soaked patch through it several times
Push a correctly sized bronze wire bore brush completely through the barrel several times, then swab with solvent again and finish with clean dry patches

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS & EJECTOR
tasks: Clean each chamber the same way you cleaned the barrel, one at a time
Clean the underside of the ejector (the "star") and the seat it drops into — trapped residue here causes hard cylinder closing and interferes with rotation
If you shoot lead, pay extra attention where the cylinder and crane join, and to the breech end of the barrel

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe all other exterior surfaces — frame, cylinder, crane — with a polymer-safe solvent and cloth
Wipe off all excess cleaner with a clean dry cloth
Ruger says it is not necessary to leave an oil residue on the frame for storage
Avoid harsh abrasives; they dull the frame coating over time

reassembly: Be certain the revolver is unloaded, and that all components and the inside of the frame are thoroughly clean.
Slip the grip over the grip post, insert the grip screw into the bottom of the grip and tighten.
fncheck: Run the manual's own function checks (p.22): the cylinder spins free without binding, the trigger is dead with the cylinder open, and the revolver dry fires cleanly several times pointed in a safe direction with every chamber confirmed empty.
